scope: Presentation of four full-range scripture excerpts (Deut 11:13-21 and Num 15:37-41, each as Hebrew and parallel PDF/HTML), rebuilt with exporter PR341 commit 1b9fdbd (a separate unmerged dependency). Visual review covered prayer pages 3 (all four PDFs) and 4 (Deut parallel, v21 continuation) and the seven browser JPGs. Mechanical claims were checked against qa.json, browser-qa.json, browser-checks.json and artifact_manifest.json.
exclusions: Acceptance of the full book, scan page, batch, service, conditionals or expanded content
Visual review of the distribution and colophon pages (generated metadata) and of the metadata/sources pages beyond confirming no heading text was inserted into the body

Source-reading and encoding acceptance: taken as approved per shema_remaining_text_qa.json (recipe and processor hashes match qa.json) and independent/shema_remaining_encoding/response.json. That record is at sources/marmorstein_rosh_hashanah_2/independent/..., not under batches/maariv_s5_s24/independent/; its status is approved and its scope excludes export.
The exporter code itself (PR341) was not reviewed here

findings.detail: The note 1 marker is in the wrong place. hebrew.tex:428 anchors \edtext{\OSInterlinearNotemark{1}} right after 'וּבְכָל־נַפְשְׁכֶֽם:' at the end of v13, which in the PDF is near the right margin of line 2. In the rendered page the '1' sits between lines 1 and 2 at about 40% of the text width from the left (around x≈325 of 935 px), next to v14 text and roughly 400 px from its anchor. The other outputs place this marker at the anchor: the Deut parallel Hebrew column (left end of line 3), the Num Hebrew PDF (after 'לֵאמֹֽר:') and the Deut Hebrew HTML (after 'נַפְשְׁכֶֽם:'). So this is a layout fault specific to this output, probably in how the zero-width raised mark interacts with right-to-left text in a full-width line. Fix it or show it is a rendering artifact, then re-render and recheck.

The raised English note markers sit noticeably to the right of their anchors: '2' is about 17 px after 'soul,' in Deut and about 28 px after 'Moses:' in Num. That suggests a space before the anchor. In the Deut parallel, the raised markers also add extra space between lines in v13, in both the English and the Hebrew column. This is cosmetic: the numbering and anchors are unambiguous.
The note markers in the body are very small and low-contrast, close to invisible at 1280 px. They are present and clickable (the AX click opened the note). This is existing exporter styling.

qa.json records rectangles and non-overlap only for the source-scan links: every one is 10.371 x 9.385 pt (at least 8 pt) and inside the 612 x 792 pt letter page. It has no field showing that every PDF link rectangle on every page was checked for minimum size, overlap and page bounds, including the citation and URL links on the metadata pages. So that claim is accepted as stated but not evidenced here. compile_warnings are [] and every *-compile-*.log hash is the empty-file SHA. I did not read the *-pdf.log files, so the 'first passes settle' claim is accepted as stated. I could not recompute any hashes; the manifest and qa.json hashes agree with each other.

verified.text_and_verse_order: Deut: 9 Hebrew/English verse pairs, 13-21, in order. In the parallel, v13-20 are on page 3 and v21 continues on page 4 with Hebrew and English still paired. Num: 5 pairs, 37-41, in order. Hebrew v37-41 is complete in the Hebrew-only PDF and HTML. The English clause splits ('soul,'/'that I will grant', 'gates,'/'so that your days') match the approved encoding.
verified.columns: Parallel PDF and HTML: Hebrew right-to-left in one column and English in the other, with paired rows aligned. No column bleed seen.
verified.notes: Hebrew outputs have 1 note ('דברים י״א:י״ג' / 'במדבר ט״ו:ל״ז'). Parallel outputs have 2: 1 Hebrew and 2 English ('Deut. XI:13' / 'Numbers XV:37'). Printed parentheses are removed and a chapter:verse colon is used. The notes contain only citations, not prayer text.
verified.english_hebrew_cues: No Hebrew cues appear in the English text.
verified.glyph_clipping: No clipped or missing glyphs seen on the reviewed pages or JPGs; qa.json reports missing_glyphs false.
verified.source_arrows: Arrows appear only where the source page changes. Deut: 1 in Hebrew (n7) and 2 in the parallel (n7 next to Hebrew, n8 next to English), with no repeated arrow on the v21 page. Num: 2 in Hebrew (n7, n9) and 4 in the parallel (n7, n8, n9, n10). In the parallel, the Hebrew n9 arrow is on v39 line 2 and the English n10 arrow on v39 line 2 of a different text position, matching the separate page breaks inside v39 recorded in the encoding approval. Verses 40-41 fall entirely after those arrows, consistent with their verse-level source being n9/n10.
verified.browser: At 1280 px, all four pages have scrollWidth 1265, so no overflow. Arrows in the parallel views sit in separate margins (x≈1122 next to Hebrew, x≈105 next to English). At 390 px, scrollWidth is 375, arrows are inline (float none) and visible in the JPG. The note popup opened and shows 'במדבר ט״ו:ל״ז'.
verified.headers_body: Running headers show only page numbers. No heading text or source-heading field appears in the body.

known_behavior_disposition.html_citation_refs_plain_text: Accepted as non-blocking existing exporter behavior. Unqualified canonical Bible URN references render as plain citation text inside the HTML notes. The notes expand and the source arrows are working links. This review does NOT claim that all citation links work.
known_behavior_disposition.pdf_citation_uri: Accepted. The PDF citation keeps href=urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:.... Note that typical PDF viewers cannot open a URN like this.
